test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Carbon forms a very large number of compounds due to two unique properties. Which of the following correctly identifies these properties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Catenation and tetravalency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon **possesses the unique ability to form **covalent bonds** with other **carbon **atoms, leading to the formation of long chains, branched chains, or even ring structures. This specific property of self-linking is known as **catenation**.
 
• Because of **catenation**, **carbon **compounds can have a variety of structures ranging from simple molecules like **methane **to complex structures like **DNA **and **proteins**. ***Hence, this property is a primary reason for the large number of carbon compounds.***
 
• **Carbon **has an **atomic number of 6** and a electronic configuration of **2, 4**, meaning it has **four valence electrons**. This characteristic is known as **tetravalency**.
 
• With **four **available electrons for bonding, **carbon **can form **four single bonds**, or combinations of **double **and **triple bonds** with other atoms such as **hydrogen**, **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, and **sulfur**. ***Hence, tetravalency allows for a vast diversity of chemical combinations.***
 
• The other options mentioned, such as **ductility**, **sonorous nature**, and **conductivity**, are primarily **physical properties** associated with metals, whereas the question asks for properties that lead to the formation of a **large number of compounds** (chemical diversity). ***Hence, option 4 is the correct identification.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isomerism in Carbon:** Apart from **catenation **and **tetravalency**, **carbon **compounds also show **isomerism**, where compounds with the same **molecular formula** possess different **structural arrangements**. This further multiplies the number of possible **carbon-based** molecules.
 
• **Bond Strength and Stability:** The **C-C bond** is exceptionally strong and stable compared to other elements. While elements like **Silicon (Si)** also show **catenation**, their chains are highly reactive and unstable because their **atomic size** is larger, making the nucleus less effective at holding shared electron pairs.
 
• **Organic Chemistry:** The study of **carbon **compounds is so vast that it constitutes a dedicated branch of science called **Organic Chemistry**. Most of the substances we use daily, such as **plastics**, **medicines**, **fuels (Petrol, Diesel)**, and **food (Carbohydrates, Fats)**, are organic compounds.
 
• **Small Atomic Size:** **Carbon **belongs to **Period 2** and **Group 14** of the **Periodic Table**. Its small **atomic radius** allows it to form multiple bonds (**double **and **triple bonds**) effectively, which larger atoms in the same group struggle to do.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Allotropy:** While not a reason for the **number of compounds**, **carbon **exists in various **allotropic forms** like **Diamond**, **Graphite**, and **Fullerenes**. **Diamond **is the hardest known natural substance, while **graphite **is a **good conductor** of electricity.
 
• **Hydrocarbons:** The simplest **carbon **compounds are **hydrocarbons**, consisting only of **carbon **and **hydrogen**. These are classified into **Saturated (Alkanes)** and **Unsaturated (Alkenes and Alkynes)** based on the types of bonds present.
 
• **Functional Groups:** The replacement of **hydrogen **atoms in a **hydrocarbon **chain with other atoms or groups (like **-OH** for **Alcohol**, **-COOH** for **Carboxylic acid**) creates different classes of **carbon **compounds with distinct chemical properties.
